prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational. Asset: production sprite atlas for Cosmic: A Sea Beneath the Moon. Input image1 is a STYLE reference only: retain the medallion form, palette, grain and physical depiction approach, but create the NEW requested subjects below. Exactly 4 columns by 3 rows, 12 circles total. Regular equal square cells, Use a landscape 4:3 canvas, exactly4 columns by3 rows of equal square cells, no outer margin. Aim2048px wide. Every circle diameter84%of its cell, centred, with generous fully transparent gutters; leave allcells complete and separated. No extra cells or objects. Original astronomical chromolithograph with dry-gouache and chalk masses: deep indigo circular fields, feathered warm-ivory light, amber heat, copper/charcoal minerals and restrained teal water. Simplify to broad meaningful structures visible at72px. Fine grain stays in subjects; generous quiet dark space. One thin ivory circular outline. No glossy UI buttons, photographic lens flare, ornamental decoration, humans, machines, text, labels, numerals, formulas or grid lines. Inside each circle the field is opaque; outside circles true alpha transparency. No shadows, rays or fragments beyond circles. Atom/particle diagrams are schematic: tiny compact ivory dots and diffuse electron-probability clouds, never planetary electron orbits; individual nuclei do NOT glow like stars. Exact invisible chemistry is communicated by game names/readings, never by invented diagnostic coloration. All terrestrial worlds have bare mineral terrain; no plants, life or modern continents. Early Moon is pale gray-ivory without familiar dark maria. All Earth cutaways are views of one continuing world.
Strict row-major subjects (left to right, then top to bottom):
1. Ejecta from later stellar generations: Two differently curved distant outflow filaments enter one common dark field, one ragged and one gentle. Avoid: Multiple sources suggested by incoming directions; no named unique solar parent.
2. A mixed interstellar element supply: Several interleaving diffuse gas wisps with a sparse field of uniform schematic nuclear motes. Avoid: Still mostly gas, no finished grains; composition is identified by label.
3. Iron-bearing metal grains: A compact loose sample of tiny angular copper-gray grains with a few sharp pale specular facets. Avoid: Microscopic representative grains, not large iron meteorites or bronze tools.
4. Silicate-forming vapor: A thin warm translucent wisp without hard contours, a few pale condensation hints at its edge. Avoid: Vapor has no solid chunks; exact silicate-forming composition needs label.
5. Silicate grains: A small loose group of angular charcoal mineral grains with dull ivory facets and broken crystalline edges. Avoid: Rocky diffuse reflection rather than shiny metal; exact mineral species not visually encoded.
6. Rock-forming dust: A loose mixed sample of dull angular mineral grains and a few metallic glints, varied sizes. Avoid: No black carbon grains or large rounded chondrules dominate yet.
7. Mixed interstellar dust: Dull mineral shards, a few metallic facets and dark carbonaceous grains form a broad loose dusty crescent. Avoid: A representative solids sample, not the much larger gas cloud.
8. A dusty interstellar cloud: A broad pale gas cloud crossed by an opaque branching charcoal dust lane. Avoid: Solid dust visibly obscures light; no bright stars or icy mantle close-up.
9. Reactive oxygen atoms: A single enlarged diffuse atomic cloud around a small compact clustered nucleus, no orbital tracks. Avoid: An atom schematic, not hot stellar bulk matter; element identity remains contextual.
10. Reactive hydrogen atoms: Two separate diffuse atom clouds, each with a single small proton centre. Avoid: Same hydrogen atoms as earlier; separated reactive participants, not a different substance.
11. A shielded cold interior: A thick dark dust arc shelters a dim interior from pale rays arriving at one outer edge. Avoid: Blocked radiation rather than a literal shell, cave or freezing weather.
12. Cold dust surfaces: Three angular dark dust grains with crisp pale edges in a quiet unlit field. Avoid: Bare cold surfaces; do not add frost before the ice chemistry.
